title: After one press of the skip link (or Back), Copy link on T12, T10 and T11 encodes the codec's reading of the bar, not the state shown: another start and relation, a bare link, or a link that cannot be read
location: site/src/lib/history.ts:218-226 (onPopState_ sets entry.current = cloneState(decodeState(location.search, tool, defaults)) before calling the tool's handler); site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:1179-1181 and 583-596 (onPopState calls readLink, which returns early when admitLink gives the state already shown, so nothing reaches stateChanged); site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:543-580 (admitLink reads g, k, c and foreign keys by rules the codec does not have); the same pattern in site/src/components/tools/T11FoldingBench.svelte:220-228 and 589, and T10GeometryStudio.svelte:590; ToolFrame.svelte:166 (the SVG/PNG footer link also comes from linkFor)
claim: history.ts replaces each instance's recorded state with the plain codec's decode on every popstate, so a tool that reads links with its own rules and finds its state unchanged keeps a recorded state that is not on screen, and linkFor (Copy link, export footer) encodes that state.
expected: SPEC 7.4: '"Copy link" always encodes the current state, whatever the address bar holds at that moment.' decisions/RT-FIX-P4-shared.md says an instance's load 'is recorded, so Copy link and the back button use it'. A same-document navigation that changes nothing on screen leaves Copy link unchanged.
observed: One press of the skip link #main fires 1 popstate; the screen does not change, but Copy link does. /tools/rep/?g=E7: before ?z=1&g=E7&c=n&s=0,0,0,0,0,0,1&w=&k=7&q=ef:7,7; after ?z=1&g=E7&c=n&s=1,1,1,1,1,1,1&w=, which reopens with the string viewer at (1,1,1,1,1,1,1). /tools/rep/?k=2: before ?z=1&g=A2&c=n&s=0,1&w=&k=2&q=ef:2,2; after ?z=1&g=A2&c=n&s=1,0&w=&k=2&q=ef:1,1 (another start and relation). /tools/rep/?g=D4&k=2: after ?z=1&g=D4&c=n&s=1,1,1,1&w=&k=2 (no q). /tools/rep/?g=A3&c=n: after ?z=1&g=A3&c=n&s=1,1,1&w= (no k, no q). M8 ?b12.k=2: after ?b12.z=1&b12.g=A3&b12.c=n&b12.s=1,0,0&b12.w=&b12.k=2&b12.q=ef:1,1, against s=0,1,0 and q=ef:2,2 on screen. /tools/rep/?k=2&m=l&w=1.1 (T12 ignores m): before ?z=1&g=A2&c=n&s=0,1&w=1.1&k=2&q=ef:2,2; after the bare /tools/rep/, which reopens to A2 node 1 with no moves. T11 /tools/fold/?g=D4&y=3.2.4.1&c=p: after ?z=1&g=D4&v=n&c=p&s=1,0,0,0&w=&y=3.2.4.1, which reopens with LINK_NOTICE and the default state. T10 /tools/geometry/?g=E8: after, the link loses r=0.0.0.0.0.0.0.1 (it reopens to the same figure). On the 11 routes whose tools use the plain codec (board, garden, form, lab, numbers, mirror, symbolic, weyl, kostant, affine, sandbox), Copy link is unchanged. The bar itself is not rewritten; the recorded state is corrected only when the reader next changes that instance.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of 006f50d plus commit 74780e4 of this branch: npm ci --prefer-offline. Unit: npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-04-p5-history.test.ts (4 failing). Browser: npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/RT-04/playwright.p5.config.ts redteam-RT-04-p5-popstate.spec.ts (5 failing: T12 on /tools/rep/ and M8 b12; each prints the Copy link before and after and the reopened state). Then PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/RT-04/playwright.p5.config.ts redteam-RT-04-p5-popstate-sweep.spec.ts (5 failing on T10, T11 and T12; 11 passing on the plain-codec tools).
specRef: SPEC.md 7.4 History API bullet ('"Copy link" always encodes the current state, whatever the address bar holds at that moment'); SPEC 6.6 Validation and URL form; decisions/RT-FIX-P4-shared.md (the recorded state is what Copy link and the back button use); DECISIONS.md P1-A2 record ('On popstate every instance re-reads the URL with decodeState against its defaults ... (plan)'), written before T10 to T12 had readers of their own.
proposedFix: In onPopState_, do not overwrite entry.current with decodeState's state. Let the tool's handler load what it shows and record that state. One way: ToolFrame records toolState after the handler, through a history.ts function that records without marking the instance changed. Another: the handler returns its admitted state. Include the export footer (linkFor) in the regression test.

reproduce.reason: Reproduced as stated; observed matches. Unit: 4 failing; after popstate linkFor gives e.g. '?z=1&g=E7&c=n&s=1,1,1,1,1,1,1&w=' against '...s=0,0,0,0,0,0,1&w=&k=7&q=ef:7,7' on screen. Browser popstate spec: 5 failing in both runs, each with 1 popstate, an unchanged screen and a different Copy link. Sweep: 5 failing (T10, T11 x2, T12 x2) and 11 passing on the plain-codec tools, in both runs. The finding's claimed level, major, is the rubric's level for a stated behaviour (SPEC 7.4 Copy link encodes the current state) that is wrong.

refute.citation: SPEC.md 7.4 History API bullet: '"Copy link" always encodes the current state, whatever the address bar holds at that moment.' This sentence is unlabelled and unqualified, and 7.4 has no [D] mark. SPEC 4.0 [D] Share and export: '"Copy link" encodes the state in the URL'. decisions/RT-FIX-P4-shared.md (second entry): an instance's load 'is recorded, so Copy link and the back button use it'. Together these support the finding's expected.
refute.evidence: Read at 006f50d (HEAD detached there; worktree clean, nothing built or run). SPEC 7.4 History API: the Copy link sentence has no 'may' or 'unless'. The only [U] in that bullet is the Safari limit. Of 7.1 to 7.9, only 7.1, 7.6 and 7.9 carry [D]. SPEC 4.0 is [D], but its text 'Copy link encodes the state in the URL' binds the builders (RED-TEAM-COMMON 2: 'unless they violated the [D] text'). Code read with git show: site/src/lib/history.ts:218-226, where onPopState_ sets entry.current = cloneState(decodeState(location.search, tool, defaults, {prefix})) and then calls the tool's callback. linkFor (197-205) encodes entry.current for the instance asked for. T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:583-596: readLink returns false when admitLink's state equals tool.state(), so nothing reaches ToolFrame's stateChanged effect (ToolFrame.svelte:106-109). The same early return is in T11FoldingBench.svelte readLink, and T10GeometryStudio.svelte applyLink returns after startLoad when the config is unchanged. t12/model.ts admitLink (543-580) drops v,m,x,t,r,j,e,y,d. It also lets g or k take that board's or node's defaults and keeps the start for c without s. decodeState has none of these rules (P1-A2: 'g without s and w' drops node and relation and gives the defaultStart). So the codec reading of ?g=E7 and ?k=2 differs from what T12 shows. Records: DECISIONS.md P1-A2 History API says 'On popstate every instance re-reads the URL with decodeState against its defaults ... (plan)'. That is a plan note on the mechanism, not a [D] passage, not a section 10 default and not an owner's answer, and it does not permit Copy link to differ from the screen. P5-A2 'panels, presets, link keys' records T12's own link rules (plan, instruction 5.10). It says nothing about the state history.ts records on popstate. Section 10 D1 to D19 has no item on links or history. The DECISIONS.md MERGE entry for the phase 4 round treats 'Copy link reopened to another state' as against SPEC 7.4. Phases: SPEC 9.1 row 1 puts URL state, history and Copy link in phase 1. T10 and T11 are phase 4 and T12 phase 5 (tool headings), so all are at or below G5. Earlier records: reports/gate-G5.md (read from claude/session-6a181f60-hzzoud; it names gate commit 006f50d) has no open item on popstate or Copy link. grep for popstate, 'back button' and 'skip link' in build-plan/reports/orchestrator/round-p4/ and round1/ finds no related record. The only popstate test at the gate commit, site/tests/unit/history.test.ts 'popstate re-reads the URL', has no regression marker and does not check linkFor after popstate. RT-04 lens section 6 excludes how a key of another tool is handled and attack 35 (absent keys meet a new board). This finding's cause is attack 22 (Copy link encodes the current state, phases 1 to 6), which the lens covers. No oracle value applies (not a mathematical claim).
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed: 7.4's Copy link sentence is unqualified and 4.0's [D] text requires the state to be encoded, so no clause permits a link that differs from the state shown. R2 failed: the finding reads 'current state' as the state on screen, as RT-FIX-P4-shared and the MERGE entry of the phase 4 round also do. R3 failed: history and Copy link are phase 1, T10 and T11 phase 4, T12 phase 5, gate G5. R4 does not apply: no mathematics is involved. R5 failed: 7.4 is not [D], and the P1-A2 '(plan)' note on popstate and P5-A2's T12 link rules are recorded mechanisms, not section 10 defaults or owner answers, and neither permits it. R6 failed: no gate-G5 open item, earlier-round record or regression test covers this cause. One weak part does not remove the cause: the T10 example's link drops r but reopens to the same figure, while the T12 and T11 examples reopen to another state or the notice. Major is the rubric's level for a stated behaviour (7.4) that is wrong.
